statement: Two ordinary $12$-hour clocks with hands are both set to the correct time, 6:00, on Monday morning. One clock gains $2$ minutes every hour, and the other loses $3$ minutes every hour. The next time the two clocks show exactly the same time, what time do they show?

choices.misconception: I worked out that the fast clock gains $4$ hours $48$ minutes, but I subtracted that from 6:00 instead of adding it.

I thought the clocks had to drift a full $24$ hours apart, so I waited $1440 \div 5 = 288$ hours. Then the fast clock had gained $9$ hours $36$ minutes and showed 3:36. A $12$-hour dial repeats after only $12$ hours.
I thought that when the two clocks agree again, they must both be showing the correct time, which is 6:00.

I thought the clocks meet when each is $6$ hours off, halfway around the dial, so the fast clock would show 6:00 plus $6$ hours. But the two clocks drift at different rates, so they are not each $6$ hours off at the same moment.

hints: Two clocks with hands show the same time when one is exactly $12$ hours ahead of the other.
The gap between the clocks grows by $2 + 3 = 5$ minutes every real hour. How long until the gap is $12$ hours?
The gap reaches $720$ minutes after $144$ hours. In that time the fast clock gains $288$ minutes, which is $4$ hours $48$ minutes.

solutions.reliable: A clock with hands repeats every $12$ hours, so the clocks agree again when the fast one is exactly $12$ hours, or $720$ minutes, ahead of the slow one. The gap grows by $2 + 3 = 5$ minutes per real hour, so this takes $720 \div 5 = 144$ real hours, which is exactly $6$ days. The real time is then 6:00 again. The fast clock has gained $144 \times 2 = 288$ minutes, which is $4$ hours $48$ minutes, so it shows 10:48. Check: the slow clock has lost $144 \times 3 = 432$ minutes, which is $7$ hours $12$ minutes, and going back $7$ hours $12$ minutes from 6:00 also lands on 10:48.
solutions.elegant: When the clocks agree, the $12$-hour gap is split between them in the ratio of their drift rates, $2 : 3$. So the fast clock is $\frac25 \times 12 = 4.8$ hours, or $4$ hours $48$ minutes, ahead of the true time. That takes $288 \div 2 = 144$ hours, a whole number of days, so the true time is 6:00 and the clocks read 10:48.
